findings.description: UP renders カチンと来る as “enrages even me.” The expression means that Ronove sometimes irritates or ticks off even Beatrice; “enrages” substantially heightens the stated emotion.

contexts.japanese:
「…お前んとこの執事、ホント口悪ぃな…」
「であろぅ？
たまに妾でもカチンと来るぞ」
「それはそれは、大変に失礼いたしました」

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice agrees that Ronove has a sharp tongue and says that even she sometimes gets irritated with him.
findings.alternative: Ronove’s insolence can provoke real anger, and Beatrice’s emphatic カチン may support a sharper English reaction than mild annoyance.

findings.description: UP says Beatrice “is sending letters to us.” The source refers to her sending this letter, singular, as the reason she must be alive; the plural invents repeated correspondence.

contexts.japanese:
「はぁ？
そりゃ生きてるに決まってるでしょう。
こうして手紙を送ってくるぐらいだもの」
「元気かどうかは別の問題だろうけどな。
肖像画の美女も、今じゃきっといいお歳だろうぜ」

The woman in that portrait must be getting up there in age by now."

The lovely woman in that portrait must be getting up there in age by now."

findings.sourceReading: Eva points to the single letter presently under discussion as apparent evidence that Beatrice is alive.
findings.alternative: The plural can be generic English for the activity of corresponding, while the scene makes clear that one particular letter triggered the discussion.
